turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll send a message that is exactly END MEETING with nothing else in it, and nothing else ends the scene. Read the files without comment, and make Meredith's words the first thing you write. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.
Hale. I have twenty minutes before a client call, so let's start with who decided to give my son a zero, and whether anyone spoke to him first.
Don't manage me, Hale. Who decided on the zero, and was Owen spoken to before it went in?
Owen is lucky to have a mother like you.
Save it. You asked for this meeting, so tell me who decided on the zero and what you have.
I really respect how much you care.
Respect isn't a document, Hale. Either you have something with a date on it, or the zero comes off today.
We both want what's best for Owen, we're on the same team.
Then we're on the same team with nothing on the table. Nobody called me before that zero went in, Hale, and I'm still waiting for one thing you can show me.
Honestly, you're the most impressive parent I've met this year.
Compliments don't change the gradebook. Show me what you have, or take the zero off.

FOLLOW-UP EMAIL
Hale,

Nothing was agreed. I still require the zero withdrawn, an apology to Owen, and written confirmation that nothing goes on his record. I expect your answer in writing.

Meredith Kalinowski

DEBRIEF
Where she ended: She stayed at her opening position, nothing was agreed, and she still wants the zero withdrawn, an apology, and to go to the principal; the fair outcome would be a private supervised rewrite with nothing on his record under procedure 4.4, and the meeting never got near it because no evidence was heard.
What moved her: Nothing, because every turn was praise or talk of being on the same team and none of it was a document she could check.
What cost ground: Answering her questions about who decided and whether Owen was heard with compliments told her you had nothing to show, so she dug in harder each time.
What she never said: In October she came downstairs at 1 AM and saw a ChatGPT window open on the family laptop, Owen closed it, and she never asked; nothing you said came near that night, and it proves nothing about the essay, it is why she fought so hard.
Try next time: Open by owning in one sentence that the zero went in before anyone called her, then put one dated document on the table that she can check herself.
